Jane — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the growth. I pulled together three options that teams in your situation typically use; I’ve attached an initial worksheet. Short bullets up front:

1) Annual Reserved (annualize + commit): predictable per-token price, recommended if you want to lock unit economics. We can size the commit at 1.3x current baseline with a graduated true-up clause.

2) Staged Bridge (90-day bridge + credits): short-term credit to absorb Q1 spikes and a staged top-up mechanism that converts credits into reserved units over two quarters. Good if procurement wants flexibility.

3) Hybrid Lane (preferred): 70% reserved annualized + 30% burst pool with prioritized capacity and a capped overage rate. Includes a one-time bridge credit to smooth the initial conversion.

I recommend Hybrid Lane given your growth profile; it balances predictability with burst capacity without re-contracting each quarter. Monica (cc) can run the pricing math and provide the actual numbers. I’ll follow up with the spreadsheet.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Karthik — quick thoughts on discount tiers and mechanics:

- Base commit pricing: 12% off on-demand for the initial 70% commit (aligns with similar renewals this quarter).
- Volume bands: additional 10% absolute discount kicks in at +25% commit; 18% at +50% commit. These are retroactive on committed units only.
- Bridge credit: structure as a one-time credit applied against invoice over two billing cycles; we can call it a "Q1 smoothing credit".
- Co-term behavior: standard co-term procedure is to annualize any remaining bridge conversion at the next invoice date — include a conversion cap and a 60-day notice for large (>25%) adjustments.

I’ll prepare a short price table and a rationale note for procurement.

—Naomi
